deep.reconstruction:
Reading order: the sheet is folded. The text begins in the right-hand column (marked 1) and continues in the left-hand column. The rotated middle text and the pencil note are archival or cover inscriptions (apparently mentioning Riemann and, probably, Hattendorff, who edited the posthumous minimal-surface memoir).

PROBLEM (right column). Find the minimal surface bounded by two circles lying in parallel planes. Riemann notes that the boundary normal direction is no longer known, so his usual method fails: one cannot map the boundary onto the sphere (Gauss map) and onto the plane eta. Instead he assumes that every section parallel to the boundary planes is a circle. With the x-axis normal to those planes, the sections are
F(x,y,z) = y^2 + z^2 + 2 alpha y + 2 beta z + gamma = 0,
where alpha, beta, gamma are functions of x (the first terms are cut off on the page; restoration mine, but certain from the next page). The task is to choose alpha, beta, gamma so the minimal condition holds.

NORMAL. Put 1/n = |grad F|. Then the unit normal is
(cos r, sin r cos phi, sin r sin phi) = n (F_x, F_y, F_z).

MINIMAL CONDITION. Riemann writes it as
d/dy (sin r cos phi) + d/dz (sin r sin phi) = 0.
Here x is regarded as a function of (y,z) on the surface, so d/dy and d/dz are total derivatives. That is, it is the divergence of the projected unit normal, equivalent to mean curvature H = 0. Using the chain rule d/dy = partial_y + x_y partial_x gives
partial_x(nF_y) x_y + partial_x(nF_z) x_z + partial_y(nF_y) + partial_z(nF_z) = 0.

CONTINUATION (next page). With x_y = -F_y/F_x and x_z = -F_z/F_x this becomes
div(n grad F) - (1/F_x) [sum_i F_i partial_x(n F_i)] = 0.
The bracket equals partial_x(n)/n^2 + (n/2) partial_x(1/n^2) = 0. So the condition is div(grad F/|grad F|) = 0, i.e. |grad F|^2 Delta F - sum_ij F_i F_j F_ij = 0.

With F_yy = F_zz = 2 and F_yz = 0, and writing G = F_y^2 + F_z^2 = 4(F + alpha^2 + beta^2 - gamma), this gives
G F_xx + 2G + 4F_x^2 - F_x partial_x G = 0.
On F = 0, with Q = alpha^2 + beta^2 - gamma (the squared radius):
Q F_xx - F_x Q' + 2Q = 0.

SPLITTING (my explicit step). F_x = 2alpha' y + 2beta' z + gamma' is linear in y and z, and a linear function vanishing on a whole circle vanishes identically. So
Q alpha'' - alpha' Q' = 0,
Q beta'' - beta' Q' = 0,
Q gamma'' - gamma' Q' + 2Q = 0.
Hence alpha'/Q and beta'/Q are constant, and gamma'/Q + 2 int dx/Q + const = 0 (the next page's first integral).

THIS PAGE (left column). Riemann's q here is -Q = gamma - alpha^2 - beta^2: the circle radius is sqrt(-q). Then:
- The centres move linearly in m = int q dx: y_c = a m - d, z_c = b m - e.
- The ODE becomes (q'/q)' = 2/q... more precisely, in terms of Q, (Q'/Q)' = 2(a^2+b^2) Q + 2/Q.
- Multiplying by Q'/Q and integrating once gives (p/q)^2 = 4/q - 4(a^2+b^2) q + 8c, with p = dq/dx and 8c the integration constant.

Substituting p = dq/dx:
- dx = dq / (2 sqrt(q [1 + 2cq - (a^2+b^2) q^2]))
- dm = q dx = q dq / (2 sqrt(q[...]))
- x = int dq/(2 sqrt(...)) and m = int q dq/(2 sqrt(...)): elliptic integrals of the first and second kind, with a cubic under the root and upper limit q.
- y = a m - d + sqrt(-q) cos psi
- z = b m - e + sqrt(-q) sin psi

Here psi is the angle of the point on its circle, so x, y, z are given as functions of the two independent variables (q, psi). Riemann then remarks that, by his general method (representing minimal surfaces through functions of a complex variable), x, y, z can be written as sums of two functions, each depending on one complex combination of the variables. The text breaks off there.

This is the derivation of the circle-foliated minimal surfaces: Riemann's minimal surfaces, with the catenoid as the special case a = b = 0.
errors: No genuine mathematical errors found. Each step checks: the chain-rule form of the minimal condition, the vanishing bracket, the reduced ODE, the first integral, and the dx and dm formulas.

Sign convention shift: the next page abbreviates alpha^2+beta^2-gamma = q (reading uncertain), but on this page q must be gamma-alpha^2-beta^2 = -(radius^2). Only then are the radius sqrt(-q), the centre law y_c = a m - d with m = int q dx, and the first integral all consistent.

Formal manipulation of square roots: writing q*sqrt(X/q) = sqrt(qX) ignores sign/branch issues. Since q<0 for real circles, one needs 1+2cq-(a^2+b^2)q^2 < 0 on the relevant range. Riemann does not discuss this.
The splitting of the PDE into three ODEs (coefficients of y, z and 1 vanish because the condition holds on a full circle) is not stated explicitly. It is valid and is used implicitly.

results.what: Minimal surface equation for an implicit surface F=0: div(grad F/|grad F|)=0, derived from the normal-vector form via the chain rule
results.modern_name: Mean curvature zero equation in level-set form
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1760)/Meusnier (1776) for graphs; level-set form classical

results.what: Minimal surfaces foliated by circles in parallel planes: centres move linearly in m=int q dx; squared radius satisfies (q'/q)^2 = 4/q - 4(a^2+b^2)q + 8c; parametrization by elliptic integrals
results.modern_name: Riemann's minimal surfaces (Riemann examples / 'staircase'), generalizing the catenoid
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, posthumously published by Hattendorff 1867 (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13; Werke); also Enneper 1869 for circle-foliated minimal surfaces

results.what: Remark that x, y, z can be expressed by the general method as sums of functions of complex variables (Weierstrass-type representation)
results.modern_name: Enneper–Weierstrass representation / Riemann's complex-function method for minimal surfaces
results.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass, Enneper (1860s); Riemann's own version in the same memoir

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft of the well-known section of Riemann's posthumous memoir on minimal surfaces (edited by Hattendorff, 1867) that introduces Riemann's minimal surfaces. The result is long credited to him. Only the manuscript details (sign conventions, order of steps) are of archival interest.

transcription_corrections: Reading order: the right-hand column (marked '1' in the margin) is the beginning of the text, and the left-hand column continues it. The machine transcription lists them in reverse.

The equation of the circular sections is truncated in the transcription; from context (and the next page) it is y^2 + z^2 + 2 alpha y + 2 beta z + gamma = 0, and 'α, β, γ für Functionen von x' is the intended reading.

On this page q denotes gamma - alpha^2 - beta^2 (the negative of the squared radius), consistent with the radius sqrt(-q); the next-page reading 'alpha^2+beta^2-gamma = q' should be checked against the image for sign.
'Ebene η' is plausible: Riemann uses an auxiliary plane η in the minimal-surface memoir.
Final line of the left column: probably 'Ausdrücke als Summen von zwei Functionen ... zweier [complex] Variablen'; it is partly illegible and cut off.
The rotated central text appears to be an address or cover note by another hand. The pencil note reads roughly 'Ms. v. Riemann über Minimalflächen ...' and may mention Hattendorff (unsure).
